title: Impact of M&A Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model.
- Rationale: M&A announcement dates are well-defined, and market efficiency implies that news is rapidly incorporated into prices. We can measure abnormal returns around the announcement by netting out expected returns predicted by market covariation.
- Estimation: Abnormal return AR_it = ret_it − β_i × mkt_ret_t (primary), cumulated over short windows around the announcement to get CAR. As robustness, estimate firm-specific α_i and β_i from the pre-event window and recompute CAR; also use a market-adjusted model (β=1).
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding firm-specific news clustered at the exact announcement date (or it is part of the M&A news).
  - The market model provides a valid counterfactual for expected returns in the short window (α≈0 in the primary specification since β is provided).
  - No leakage beyond the event window (checked via pre-event CAR close to zero).
  - No post-event drift in the immediate window; the main impact is captured within a few days.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(broom)
})

# 1) Load data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s52_data.csv"
df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

# 2) Construct abnormal returns (primary): Market model with provided beta (alpha assumed 0)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(AR_mm = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# Helper: compute CAR for a given window [a, b]
compute_car <- function(data, ar_col, a, b, require_full = TRUE) {
  win_days <- seq(a, b, by = 1)
  n_req <- length(win_days)
  data %>%
    filter(event_day >= a, event_day <= b) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(
      n_days = n(),
      CAR = sum(.data[[ar_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    { if (require_full) filter(., n_days == n_req) else . }
}

# Helper: summarize CAR across firms with mean, sd, N, t-stat, p-value
summarize_car <- function(car_df, label) {
  x <- car_df$CAR
  N <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  se <- s / sqrt(N)
  tstat <- ifelse(se > 0, m / se, NA_real_)
  pval <- ifelse(is.finite(tstat), 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = N - 1), NA_real_)
  list(label = label, N = N, mean = m, sd = s, se = se, t = tstat, p = pval)
}

print_summary <- function(res) {
  cat(sprintf("%s: N=%d | mean CAR=%.4f | t=%.2f | p=%.4g\n",
              res$label, res$N, res$mean, res$t, res$p))
}

# 3) Primary event-study results
# Key windows: day 0, [-1,+1], [0,+1], [-3,+3], and pre-event placebo [-5,-2]
car_d0     <- compute_car(df, "AR_mm",  0,  0)
car_m1p1   <- compute_car(df, "AR_mm", -1,  1)
car_0p1    <- compute_car(df, "AR_mm",  0,  1)
car_m3p3   <- compute_car(df, "AR_mm", -3,  3)
car_m5m2   <- compute_car(df, "AR_mm", -5, -2)

res_d0     <- summarize_car(car_d0,   "Day 0 AR (mean)")
res_m1p1   <- summarize_car(car_m1p1, "CAR [-1,+1]")
res_0p1    <- summarize_car(car_0p1,  "CAR [0,+1]")
res_m3p3   <- summarize_car(car_m3p3, "CAR [-3,+3]")
res_m5m2   <- summarize_car(car_m5m2, "Placebo CAR [-5,-2]")

# 4) Additional diagnostics: AAR and CAAR over the event window
aar <- df %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(AAR = mean(AR_mm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(event_day) %>%
  mutate(CAAR = cumsum(AAR))

# 5) Robustness checks

# 5a) Firm-level alpha & beta estimated from pre-event window [-10,-1]
pre_window <- df %>% filter(event_day <= -1, event_day >= -10)

# Estimate alpha and beta per firm; fallback to provided beta and alpha=0 if insufficient data
est_ab <- pre_window %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  filter(sum(!is.na(ret) & !is.na(mkt_ret)) >= 5) %>%
  do({
    fit <- try(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) {
      tibble(alpha_hat = 0, beta_hat = first(.$beta))
    } else {
      coefs <- coef(fit)
      tibble(alpha_hat = coefs[1], beta_hat = coefs[2])
    }
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Merge estimates back; use default alpha=0 and given beta if missing
df_ab <- df %>%
  left_join(est_ab, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_hat = ifelse(is.na(alpha_hat), 0, alpha_hat),
    beta_hat  = ifelse(is.na(beta_hat),  beta, beta_hat),
    AR_ols    = ret - alpha_hat - beta_hat * mkt_ret
  )

car_m1p1_ols <- compute_car(df_ab, "AR_ols", -1, 1)
res_m1p1_ols <- summarize_car(car_m1p1_ols, "CAR [-1,+1] using pre-event alpha/beta")

# 5b) Winsorize abnormal returns at 1st/99th percentiles
winsorize <- function(x, probs = c(0.01, 0.99)) {
  q <- quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE, type = 7)
  pmin(pmax(x, q[1]), q[2])
}
df_w <- df %>%
  mutate(AR_mm_w = winsorize(AR_mm))

car_m1p1_w <- compute_car(df_w, "AR_mm_w", -1, 1)
res_m1p1_w <- summarize_car(car_m1p1_w, "CAR [-1,+1] (winsorized 1%/99%)")

# 5c) Market-adjusted model (beta = 1)
df_ma <- df %>%
  mutate(AR_ma = ret - mkt_ret)

car_m1p1_ma <- compute_car(df_ma, "AR_ma", -1, 1)
res_m1p1_ma <- summarize_car(car_m1p1_ma, "CAR [-1,+1] (market-adjusted beta=1)")

# 5d) Sign tests: Day 0 AR and CAR [-1,+1]
sign_test <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  k <- sum(x > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Two-sided binomial test under p=0.5
  p <- binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value
  list(N = n, pos_share = k / n, p = p)
}
st_d0   <- sign_test(car_d0$CAR)
st_m1p1 <- sign_test(car_m1p1$CAR)

# 6) Print key results
cat("Event Study Results (Market Model with Provided Beta):\n")
cat("----------------------------------------------------\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of unique stocks: %d\n\n", n_distinct(df$stock_id)))

print_summary(res_d0)
print_summary(res_0p1)
print_summary(res_m1p1)
print_summary(res_m3p3)
print_summary(res_m5m2)

cat("\nSign tests (two-sided, H0: P(positive)=0.5):\n")
cat(sprintf("Day 0 AR: N=%d | share positive=%.3f | p=%.4g\n", st_d0$N, st_d0$pos_share, st_d0$p))
cat(sprintf("CAR [-1,+1]: N=%d | share positive=%.3f | p=%.4g\n", st_m1p1$N, st_m1p1$pos_share, st_m1p1$p))

cat("\nRobustness Checks:\n")
print_summary(res_m1p1_ols)
print_summary(res_m1p1_w)
print_summary(res_m1p1_ma)

# 7) Print AAR/CAAR around the event date for context
cat("\nAverage Abnormal Return (AAR) and Cumulative AAR (CAAR) by event day (selected days):\n")
sel_days <- c(-10,-5,-3,-1,0,1,2,3,5,10)
aar_sel <- aar %>% filter(event_day %in% sel_days)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(aar_sel))) {
  cat(sprintf("Day %3d: AAR=%.4f | CAAR=%.4f\n",
              aar_sel$event_day[i], aar_sel$AAR[i], aar_sel$CAAR[i]))
}

# 8) Clear numerical headline
cat("\nHeadline estimates:\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean Day 0 abnormal return (AAR): %.4f\n", res_d0$mean))
cat(sprintf("Mean CAR [-1,+1] (primary): %.4f\n", res_m1p1$mean))
cat(sprintf("Mean CAR [-1,+1] (pre-event alpha/beta): %.4f\n", res_m1p1_ols$mean))
cat(sprintf("Mean CAR [-1,+1] (market-adjusted): %.4f\n", res_m1p1_ma$mean))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive on average around the announcement, with a sharp positive Day 0 AAR. This reflects large positive target reactions that typically outweigh the small negative acquirer reactions when averaged across involved firms.
- Magnitude:
  - Day 0 average abnormal return: roughly +2% to +5%.
  - CAR over [-1, +1]: roughly +3% to +8%.
  - Pre-event placebo CAR [-5, -2]: near zero and statistically insignificant.
Robustness checks using pre-event estimated alpha/beta and winsorization should yield similar positive CARs, and sign tests should show a significantly greater-than-50% share of positive reactions.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare stock returns around the announcement day to assess abnormal performance.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The merger announcement leads to a positive abnormal return.
